digest: A workstation (WS-FIN-09) in the finance subnet was compromised via a phishing attachment, leading to the execution of an encoded PowerShell script that established a Cobalt Strike command and control (C2) beacon to a known malicious domain and IP address.

evidence_findings.title: Initial Access via Phishing Attachment
evidence_findings.subject: WS-FIN-09
evidence_findings.evidence: An alert for 'Suspicious Execution via Phishing Attachment' was triggered, showing 'excel.exe' spawning 'powershell.exe' on WS-FIN-09.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The initial compromise occurred through a user opening a malicious attachment, likely delivered via phishing.

evidence_findings.title: Encoded PowerShell Execution
evidence_findings.subject: powershell.exe
evidence_findings.evidence: The process 'powershell.exe' was executed with the command line 'powershell.exe -NonI -W Hidden -EncodedCommand <BASE64_PAYLOAD>'. Analysis of the decoded payload indicated an attempt to download from a remote domain using 'IEX Net.WebClient'.
evidence_findings.conclusion: A malicious, encoded PowerShell script was executed to evade detection and download a secondary payload.

evidence_findings.title: Command and Control Beaconing
evidence_findings.evidence: Firewall logs show persistent outbound TLS traffic from WS-FIN-09 (10.20.4.115) to 198.51.100.44 on port 443, with periodic 30-second interval pulses, consistent with C2 beaconing.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The compromised host established a persistent command and control channel to an external server.

evidence_findings.title: Malicious C2 Infrastructure Identified
evidence_findings.subject: stage2.malicious-domain.xyz / 198.51.100.44
evidence_findings.evidence: Threat intelligence enrichment identified 'stage2.malicious-domain.xyz' as a malicious domain with a reputation score of 89/100, resolved via Fast Flux DNS. This IOC also matches a US-CERT advisory bulletin.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The C2 infrastructure used by the attacker is known to be malicious and associated with threat activity.

attack_chain.description: A user on WS-FIN-09 opened a malicious attachment, likely from a phishing email.
Microsoft Excel spawned PowerShell, which executed a hidden, encoded command.
The use of an encoded PowerShell command was intended to obfuscate malicious activity and bypass security controls.
The PowerShell script established a persistent C2 beacon to 'stage2.malicious-domain.xyz' (198.51.100.44) over TLS.

attack_timeline.attack_behavior: Suspicious process execution (excel.exe -> powershell.exe) detected on WS-FIN-09.
Outbound beacon traffic detected from WS-FIN-09 to 198.51.100.44.
Analysis reveals encoded PowerShell payload attempts download from remote domain.
Host network isolation approved for WS-FIN-09.

ioc_indicators.context: C2 beacon domain, resolved via Fast Flux DNS, 89/100 Malicious reputation.
C2 server IP address, destination for persistent outbound TLS traffic.
Malicious PowerShell execution pattern used for payload download.

remediations.description: Isolate host WS-FIN-09 from the network to prevent further compromise or lateral movement.
Block the malicious domain 'stage2.malicious-domain.xyz' and IP address '198.51.100.44' at all network perimeter devices (firewalls, DNS servers, proxies).
Initiate forensic analysis on WS-FIN-09 to determine the full extent of compromise, followed by re-imaging the system.
Conduct targeted phishing awareness training for the affected user and the finance department.

unknowns: The full decoded content of the PowerShell payload beyond the IEX Net.WebClient download attempt.
